title: Ventilator safety checks

objectives: Check and record ventilator values at the frequency set by policy and whenever the patient changes.
Respond to every alarm by going to the patient and securing ventilation first.
Know that settings and alarm limits are changed only with authority.

items.text: Applies to every ventilated patient at every shift check and after any change in the patient.

Respond to every alarm by going to the patient; do not rely on silencing. If ventilation is inadequate and the cause is not immediately correctable, use the unit's emergency ventilation method and call for help.
Do not change alarm limits or modes unless authorised by order, protocol and training; extreme limits make alarms useless.

Compare set and delivered tidal volume and note leaks; check circuit and cuff problems per policy; report asynchrony; do not change tidal volume, PEEP or other settings unless a local protocol and your competence allow it.
Who may change settings and alarm limits is set by protocol and competence; the AARC guideline does not say who performs assessments.
Device-specific alarm behaviour (reset, silence, priority) differs between manufacturers: use the manual for your device and software version only per your unit's documentation standard.
ESICM 2023 recommendations apply to ARDS only; do not generalise ARDS-specific measures (such as prone positioning or neuromuscular blockade) to all ventilated patients.
Routine check sequence (settings, circuit, humidification, alarms) follows the unit's checklist; no cross-manufacturer source was read.
Record set and delivered values, airway pressures, SpO2, end-tidal CO2 and waveforms at the policy frequency, and trends.
Call for help early for rising pressures, falling volumes, desaturation or distress.
Record values, checks, alarms and responses per unit standard.

checklist.text: Look at the patient first: work of breathing, chest movement, colour, SpO2.
Compare set and delivered tidal volume and look for leaks.
Confirm alarms are on and limits are as ordered or per protocol; do not alter limits without authority.
Check circuit connections and the cuff per the unit's checklist.
If ventilation is inadequate and not quickly correctable, use the unit's emergency ventilation method and call for help.
Record settings, delivered values and any alarm and response.
